title: data-leash-exception-patterns-and-customer-fallthrough-notes
summary: Working notes on a lightweight exceptions model were calling 'data leash' — patterns where tenant data is tethered to the pinned region but may be allowed (or forced) to fall through to another region for specific, auditable reasons. Purpose: capture concrete patterns, telemetry hooks, operator steps, billing implications, and suggested customer messaging.
background: Motivation: full hard-pinning for every tenant imposes cost and operational friction. Several real customer scenarios (third-party connectors, legacy webhooks, emergency forensics, real-time third-party scoring) require occasional, controlled cross-region access. We need a repeatable, auditable exceptions model that minimizes risk and supports compliance reporting.
scope: This doc focuses on: (1) exception classes that are acceptable vs. not acceptable; (2) routing/fallback strategies and their guarantees; (3) telemetry and evidence capture; (4) operator and legal artifacts to support audits; (5) cost attribution and customer-facing wording. NOT in scope: detailed KMS/HSM key workflows (refer to security-led spec).
key_definitions: data leash: a timeboxed, policy-attested allowance for a tenant's request or dataset to be served or routed outside of the tenants pinned region. leash token: a signed metadata token attached to the request indicating exception reason, TTL, and approving actor. fallthrough: the actual routing of data/request to a non-pinned region. auditable-evidence: minimal trace bundle (request id, leash token, operator id or automation id, timestamp, destination region, TTL, sampled payload hash).
exception_patterns:
1) Connector-Proxy Exception:
   - When a customer configures an external SaaS connector (e.g., CRM webhook) that only has endpoints in a different geography and customer accepts cross-border transfer in contract.
   - Controls: pre-approved connector in account profile, automation issues leash token with 1-hour TTL, incremental charges flagged.

2) Emergency Forensics Exception:
   - Security incident requires short-term export for investigator in another region.
   - Controls: requires two approvers (oncall+security lead), leash token 24 hours, full payload hashed and stored in evidence bucket, legal notified.

3) Low-sensitivity Aggregation Exception:
   - Non-PII aggregated telemetry or ML features used by global model training.
   - Controls: default allowed if dataset marked non-sensitive and hashed, daily rollup only, automation TTL 72h.

4) Latency-fallback for SLA-critical inference:
   - If pinned region capacity exhausted and customer has failover SLA, route to nearest available region with telemetry capture and customer-configured opt-in.
   - Controls: route only to pre-approved regions, immediate billing flag, optional customer notification header.

5) Disallowed patterns:
   - Permanent un-audited replication of tenant data across borders, ad-hoc manual downloads without evidence, use by third parties without contractual consent.
detection_and_telemetry:
Minimum telemetry events to emit for every leash/fallthrough:
- LEASH_ISSUED (token_id, tenant_id, reason_code, issued_by, ttl_seconds, originating_region)
- LEASH_APPLIED (token_id, request_id, dest_region, route_decision_reason, fallback_policy_id)
- LEASH_EXPIRED (token_id, timestamp)
- LEASH_AUDIT_BUNDLE_CREATED (token_id, evidence_bucket_path, hash)
All events should include sampling flags, but audit bundles must be stored un-sampled for 90 days (or longer if contract). Tag events with billing_token to enable chargeback. Correlate with request traces and KV cache annotations.
Alerting: anomalous rate of LEASH_APPLIED (> x% of requests for tenant) -> create ticket to account owner and solutions engineering.
fallthrough_routing_options:
A) Policy-first routing: enforce allow-list of destination regions per tenant; deny by default.
B) Capacity-fallback routing: auto-allow to tiered regions if capacity threshold exceeded (configured per-tenant).
C) Manual operator override: one-off operator-issued leash tokens via internal tooling (requires 2FA and approver logging).
For each option capture: guarantee level (latency/cost/audit), who can trigger, TTL, and whether customer gets billed differently.
audit_and_evidence: Evidence bundle contents (minimal): request headers (masked), leash token, request id, originating region, destination region, operator/automation ID, timestamp, consent artifact id (if applicable), SHA256 of payload, storage path for sampled payloads. Retention: default 90 days; for enterprise contracts support up to 7 years. Evidence access controlled by legal/incident teams; create read-only audit views in console referencing bundle ids.
cost_accounting:
Charge model recommendations:
- Per-leash flat surcharge + per-token (or compute) delta when routed to non-pinned region.
- Tag billing records with leash_token to enable rollback or credits if exception was operator error.
- Monthly summary report for tenants showing counts, cost deltas, and reason categories.
Operational note: estimate 1% of requests as leash upper bound for standard customers; run simulation before enabling broad policies.
operator_runbook:
Quick steps for one-off operator-issued leash (emergency):
1) Create ticket in JIRA with tenant id, reason, and expected TTL.
2) Get second approver (security or account lead) to comment on ticket.
3) Use internal /admin/leash-issue UI: select tenant, reason_code, TTL, destination region. UI will generate leash_token and evidence bucket id.
4) Add ticket link and leash_token to the audit bundle.
5) Monitor LEASH_APPLIED events for the tenant for next 24h and escalate if >5% spike.
6) After TTL expiry, verify LEASH_EXPIRED and close ticket with link to audit bundle.
Checklist: confirm legal waiver if needed; record cost center for chargeback.
customer_communications:
Suggested customer wording (console + email):
- Console flag: "Cross-region exceptions enabled for approved connectors and emergency forensics. All exceptions are timeboxed and logged; see audit center for details."
- Email template (opt-in): "We may route select requests to an alternate region to maintain availability or support third-party integrations. These events are recorded and can be disabled in account settings; contact support for contract-level controls."
Provide an opt-out flow for strict-pin customers and a demo video for enterprise legal teams showing evidence artifacts.
unresolved_questions:
- Default TTL values: should we standardize (1h/24h/72h) or keep per-policy?
- Evidence retention policy by region (some jurisdictions require shorter retention).
- Integrations with KMS for evidence encryption-at-rest across regions.
- Billing UI design to show leash charges per-route at token granularity.
- Should we surface LEASH events in customer-facing telemetry in a limited way?
references: Links: CONFLUENCE-RESIDENCY-9876 (policy baseline), PRIV-PIN-SPEC-v2 (internal spec), JIRA-PRIVPIN-412 (policy epic), github ops PR 201. See also security-led notes on cross-region key handling.
